title: Devnet-9 raises blob throughput and changes the fee market
summary: Devnet-9 doubles the target blob count per block and introduces a separate blob base fee curve.
content:
SAMPLE FIXTURE - synthetic data for local dry-runs, not real news.

Devnet-9 is live. The target blob count per block moves from 6 to 12 with a maximum of 18, and the blob base fee now uses its own update fraction so L2 data costs decouple from execution gas.

What changed:
- Target blobs per block: 6 -> 12 (max 9 -> 18).
- Blob base fee update fraction tuned so a sustained 2x demand spike settles in roughly 12 blocks instead of 30.
- Client teams must update to the devnet-9 releases; older clients will fork off.

For rollup operators: expect lower and less spiky data costs, but re-tune your blob submission strategy - posting one blob per batch is no longer the cheapest option in most cases.

title: Local fee markets get per-account congestion pricing
summary: Priority fees become account-scoped, so congestion on one program stops repricing the whole block.
content:
SAMPLE FIXTURE - synthetic data for local dry-runs, not real news.

Local fee markets now price congestion per writable account rather than per block. A hot NFT mint no longer raises the priority fee required for unrelated transfers.

What changed:
- Priority fee estimation is account-scoped; RPC getRecentPrioritizationFees returns per-account percentiles.
- Wallets that used a single global fee estimate will overpay; update to the account-aware estimate.
- Measured on testnet: median priority fee for unrelated transfers during a mint event fell 71%.

title: Batched Recursive Proofs for Rollup Settlement
summary: Abstract: A batching scheme for recursive SNARKs that cuts settlement proof cost per transaction by 3.4x at a fixed verifier gas budget.
content:
SAMPLE FIXTURE - synthetic data for local dry-runs, not real news.

Abstract:
We present a batching scheme for recursive SNARK settlement proofs. By deferring the final aggregation step and sharing the verifier circuit across batches, per-transaction proving cost drops 3.4x at a fixed on-chain verification gas budget. We provide a security argument in the algebraic group model and an open-source prototype.

title: An onchain payments SDK with sponsored gas
summary: New SDK bundles account abstraction paymasters so apps can sponsor user transaction fees.
content:
SAMPLE FIXTURE - synthetic data for local dry-runs, not real news.

A new payments SDK wraps ERC-4337 paymasters so applications can sponsor user gas without running their own bundler.

What changed:
- Sponsored transactions are a two-line SDK call instead of a custom paymaster deployment.
- Per-app spend caps and per-user rate limits are enforced server side.
- Supported on two L2s at launch; more to follow. Fees are quoted in the app's settlement currency.
